s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of skin necrosis with respiratory failure and bacteremia
salient_findings: Erythema and edematous necrotic plaques of the bilateral ears
Necrosis progressed to involve earlobe and helix
Biopsy showed full-thickness necrosis with sparse inflammation and adnexal epithelia necrosis
key_facts: Patient has a medical history of factor VII deficiency hemophilia
Presented with acute hypoxic respiratory failure
Intubated with prone positioning
Developed Staphylococcus hemolyticus bacteremia
Erythematous plaques and edematous necrotic lesions on bilateral ears
No devices had been used on the ears
Necrosis progressed over time
Biopsy showed detached epidermis with full-thickness necrosis
Biopsy showed necrosis of adnexal epithelia, including folliculosebaceous units and eccrine glands

shortlist.label: Purpura fulminans
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of skin necrosis with respiratory failure and bacteremia

shortlist.label: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a medical history of factor VII deficiency hemophilia and developed skin necrosis

shortlist.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with acute hypoxic respiratory failure and developed Staphylococcus hemolyticus bacteremia

shortlist.label: Ecthyma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed erythematous plaques and edematous necrotic lesions on bilateral ears with Staphylococcus hemolyticus bacteremia

shortlist.label: Coumadin necrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a medical history of factor VII deficiency hemophilia and developed skin necrosis, possibly related to anticoagulant therapy

raw.rationale: The patient's history of factor VII deficiency hemophilia and the development of erythematous plaques and edematous necrotic lesions on the bilateral ears, particularly with full-thickness necrosis and necrosis of adnexal epithelia, are consistent with warfarin-induced skin necrosis, which is a known complication in patients with protein C or protein S deficiency, but can also occur in those with other coagulopathies like factor VII deficiency when initiated on warfarin.

rejected.label: Purpura fulminans
rejected.why: While purpura fulminans can cause skin necrosis, it is typically associated with severe infection and disseminated intravascular coagulation, which, although possible, is not the most direct explanation given the biopsy findings and the specific pattern of skin lesions.

rejected.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
rejected.why: DIC can cause skin lesions due to microthrombi formation, but the specific pattern of full-thickness necrosis and the involvement of adnexal structures point more towards a direct effect of anticoagulation on skin, as seen in warfarin-induced skin necrosis.

rejected.label: Ecthyma gangrenosum
rejected.why: Ecthyma gangrenosum is typically associated with Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia and presents with distinct gangrenous lesions, which does not match the patient's Staphylococcus hemolyticus bacteremia and the description of the lesions.

rejected.label: Coumadin necrosis
rejected.why: Coumadin necrosis is another term for warfarin-induced skin necrosis, thus it's essentially the same condition as the chosen champion, not a distinct alternative to reject.

rejected.label: Purpura fulminans
rejected.why: Already addressed in the rejection of Purpura fulminans
